reasons: Cited Section 14.3 selects California law, which is expressly within the rule's accepted set (fallback: Delaware or California law and courts), and the deterministic check confirms the governing law is in-scope.

The dispute forum is domestic — AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County, California, with enforcement in California courts — so it does not implicate the walk-away triggers (non-accepted home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or arbitration seated abroad); the rule frames its arbitration objection as foreign arbitration.

Classification as compliant-at-fallback is consistent with the playbook's semantics: the shortfall from preferred (New York law/New York County courts) and the substitution of binding domestic arbitration for a pure court forum are sub-elements properly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline text was changed and no counterparty comment was raised; the rationale accurately restates the clause (law, seat, arbitrator, enforcement venue) with no material mischaracterization.
